name: Forsaken
summary: Across Azeroth, intelligent undead called the Forsaken live beneath Lordaeron's ruined capital in the Undercity. They broke from the Scourge after the Third War under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Though mistrusted, they hold a wary alliance with the Horde.

sections.title: Broken Shackles
sections.body:
After the Third War, the Lich King's hold weakened. Thousands of undead in Lordaeron's blighted ruins regained their minds and memories, and recalled the slaughter they had been forced to commit. The living hunted them, though they had once been citizens of Lordaeron.

Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, Quel'Thalas's fallen ranger-general, had become an unholy banshee. She gathered the wandering undead and claimed the catacombs beneath Capital City. There she named their new nation the Forsaken.

sections.title: An Alliance of Convenience
sections.body:
Enemies surrounded the Forsaken, above all the Scarlet Crusade and the Scourge. Lady Sylvanas sent emissaries in search of allies. Across the Great Sea, tauren elders urged compassion, believing the cursed people might find redemption or a cure through the earth.

Warchief Thrall had misgivings, but the Horde accepted the Forsaken. In return, the Horde gained a vital foothold in the north of the Eastern Kingdoms.

sections.title: Dark Laboratories
sections.body:
The Forsaken seek their own survival while presenting a cooperative face to their allies in Kalimdor. Beneath the Undercity, the Royal Apothecary Society works in the Apothecarium to create a New Plague potent enough to destroy both the Scourge and living threats.

Forsaken champions such as Nathanos Blightcaller wage bitter wars across the Plaguelands, Hillsbrad Foothills, and the Scarlet Monastery. They fight to secure their sovereign borders.

faq.q: Are the Forsaken part of the Scourge?
faq.answer: No. The Forsaken broke free from the Lich King's mental domination after the Third War. They loathe the Scourge, regard Arthas as their absolute mortal enemy, and bitterly fight his minions throughout the Plaguelands.

The Forsaken capital is the Undercity, a vast sprawl beneath the ruins of Capital City in Tirisfal Glades. Sylvanas's forces expanded the royal crypts and sewers into a fortified sanctuary safe from the light and outdoor threats.

faq.q: Why did the Horde let the Forsaken join?
faq.answer: The tauren urged the Horde to accept the Forsaken, seeing a chance for redemption and hoping the earth's powers might cure their affliction. Magatha Grimtotem also supported the pact. Warchief Thrall agreed because the Horde urgently needed a military foothold in the Eastern Kingdoms.

Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the Banshee Queen, rules the Forsaken. Once a high elven ranger-general, she fell defending Silvermoon and freed the undead who had regained their own will. She rules from the Undercity with her dreadlord advisor, Varimathras.

faq.q: Are the Forsaken all former humans?
faq.answer: Most Forsaken were once humans of Lordaeron, slain and raised during the Scourge invasion. Their leaders include former elves such as Sylvanas. Anyone who bends the knee to the Dark Lady is welcomed into their ranks.

faq.q: Why does the Scarlet Crusade hate the Forsaken so much?
faq.answer: The Scarlet Crusade makes no distinction between mindful Forsaken and mindless Scourge. Its zealots see all undead as abominations to be purged with fire and holy wrath, whatever their will or allegiance.

faq.q: Which classes can the Forsaken be?
faq.answer: The Forsaken train as warriors, paladins, rogues, priests, mages, and warlocks. Their paladins still wield the Holy Light, though it burns their dead flesh.

angles.text: As one of the Forsaken, you walk the earth in rotting flesh, cursed and spurned by former kin. Your people are bound together under the Dark Lady as they carve out an empire of their own.
Your elders championed the Forsaken's place in the Horde out of sympathy. They hoped your shamanic and druidic rites might soothe or heal the Forsaken's tragic condition.
To the Alliance, the Forsaken are nightmarish parodies of fallen friends and family from Lordaeron. They hold former imperial lands and answer overtures with poison and steel.

Thrall forged an alliance of convenience with the Undercity to secure territory in the East. Many orcs and trolls view the Forsaken's grim apothecary experiments and necromantic culture with deep suspicion.
